dial.summary: Macro backdrop constructive and incrementally improving as of August 23: ISM Manufacturing holds at 55.6% (7-month expansion streak), 2s10s steepening to +51bps, real yields showing first 4-week down tick (2.44% July 23 TIPS auction → 2.35% Aug 20), and Fed balance sheet stable at $6.75T; DXY continues its 30-day downtrend (100.75 → 98.84) but remains in the neutral band; BTC at $77,416 with BTC.D firm at 59.3% and TOTAL ~$2.74T confirm accumulation conditions with funding near zero and stablecoin dominance compressing — the decisive PCE (Aug 26), GDP 2nd estimate (Aug 26), and Warsh Jackson Hole keynote (Aug 28) are the next macro gates before FOMC September 15–16.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) carried at ~$102.7T — July aggregate not yet published (~6-week reporting lag); US M2 confirmed at $23.16T for June 2026, +5.6% YoY (record high, 28th consecutive monthly increase); no YoY contraction signal from any major central bank; 4-week trend up based on sustained US M2 expansion and continued global central bank balance sheet stability; status supportive (4-week uptrend confirmed; YoY contraction headwind condition not triggered).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent reading — August 2026 data releases September 1, 2026; sub-indexes: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8% (first factory hiring expansion in 18 months), Prices Paid 71.1%; July reading is the highest since May 2022; 4-week trend up: June 53.3% → July 55.6% = +2.3pp; status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 98.84 on August 23, 2026; 4-week trend down: DXY was ~100.75–101.51 around July 22–27 → 98.84 on August 23 = approximately -1.9%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; structural dollar weakness driven by US Treasury's expanded long-term buyback program and rate cut expectations; status NEUTRAL (ICE DXY in the 97.5–100 neutral band; a sustained close below 97.5 would flip to supportive; PCE August 26 and Warsh Jackson Hole keynote August 28 are key directional catalysts).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.35% as of August 20–21, 2026; 4-week trend down: 10-year TIPS auction cleared at 2.438% on July 23, 2026 → DFII10 at 2.35% on August 20 = -9bps, above the 5bps flat threshold; trend has reversed from prior 'up' read; status headwind (above the 2% absolute threshold despite falling trend; a soft PCE on August 26 and dovish Warsh keynote August 28 are the catalysts needed to compress real yields meaningfully below 2%).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 22, 2026: 10Y yield closed at 4.74% (up from 4.71% prior session); 2Y yield approximately 4.23% (interpolated from latest confirmed DGS2 at 4.15% on August 13 and the ~+0.51% spread corroborated by multiple sources); spread = +51bps; 4-week trend up: ~+35bps (July 21) → +51bps (August 23) = +16bps steepening, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (positive spread AND sustained 4-week steepening trend intact; PCE August 26 and Warsh tone August 28 are the next key curve inputs).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,745,699M (~$6.75T) for week ending August 19, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 20); down ~$10B from $6.76T the prior week (August 12); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (August 5) → $6.75T (August 19) = +$50B (+0.7%), near the 0.5% flat threshold; balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT signal; status supportive.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate near zero at approximately +0.0025%/8h on August 21, 2026; funding briefly dipped negative on August 22 as BTC surged to $77,416 (+22% weekly, biggest weekly rally in 3 years) — driven by spot ETF inflows ($517M+) and institutional demand rather than leveraged retail; this is a textbook accumulation signature (price up, funding flat-to-negative); well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; 30-day trend down vs late-June/early-July levels; CoinGlass direct fetch blocked, funding rate value based on confirmed secondary search data.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$308B (CoinGecko/CoinMarketCap, August 13, 2026); total crypto market cap ~$2.64–2.74T (BTC at $77,416 with 59.3% dominance as of August 22); stablecoin dominance ~11.2–11.7% depending on TOTAL benchmark; 30-day trend down: ~14.3% (mid-July) → ~12.5% (early August) → ~11.0–11.7% (August 23) — compressed as capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets accelerating during BTC's 22% weekly surge; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — dominance rising while TOTAL rises — is opposite of current dynamics).

upcoming.title: Consumer Confidence (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — first consumer sentiment read incorporating July NFP shock (−23K), hot core CPI (3.1%), FOMC Minutes (August 19), Flash PMI (August 21), and BTC's 22% weekly surge to $77,416 (biggest weekly rally in 3 years as of August 22); a sharp deterioration in confidence would raise Q3 recession risk and bolster the case for September rate cuts; precedes the decisive PCE/GDP cluster the following morning.

upcoming.title: PCE Price Index (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA Personal Income and Outlays at 8:30 AM ET — July PCE Price Index (Fed's preferred inflation gauge), Personal Income, and Personal Spending; arrives one day before Jackson Hole opens; hot core CPI (3.1% YoY, August 12) implies core PCE potentially 2.7–2.8% YoY; a reading above 2.8% strongly supports a September hike; a soft print (<2.5%) preserves the rate-cut path, reinforces BTC Accumulation, and could push DXY below 97.5 from current 98.84 — the single most important data print ahead of Jackson Hole.

upcoming.title: GDP 2nd Estimate (Q2 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA releases the second estimate of Q2 2026 GDP at 8:30 AM ET alongside July PCE, one day before Jackson Hole opens; July NFP shock (−23K) and hot core CPI (3.1%) have raised Q3 recession concerns; significant downward revisions alongside soft labor and hot inflation would reinforce the stagflation narrative and set the tone for Warsh's keynote the following morning.

upcoming.title: Jackson Hole Economic Symposium Opens (August 27–29)
upcoming.note: Kansas City Fed annual Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium begins at Jackson Lake Lodge, Wyoming — runs August 27–29 (Thursday–Saturday); theme: 'Financial Innovation: Implications for Payments and Policy'; by the time proceedings open, markets will have processed PCE (August 26), GDP Q2 2nd estimate (August 26), Consumer Confidence (August 25), Flash PMI (August 21), and BTC's historic 22% weekly rally to $77,416; Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole keynote Friday morning August 28; FOMC September 15–16 is the next binding commitment.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 22, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 22, 2026 — released the opening morning of Jackson Hole; a sustained rise in claims arriving as Jackson Hole opens would immediately shape the tone for Fed Chair Warsh's inaugural keynote the next morning (August 28); context: July NFP shocked at −23K, making weekly claims particularly closely watched.

upcoming.title: Fed Chair Warsh Inaugural Jackson Hole Keynote
upcoming.note: Kevin Warsh delivers his inaugural Jackson Hole address Friday morning August 28 — the single most important macro event of this cycle for the crypto risk framework; by August 28 all macro inputs will be in hand (PCE August 26, GDP 2nd estimate August 26, Consumer Confidence August 25, Flash PMI August 21); real yields are showing a first 4-week downtrend (2.44% July 23 → 2.35% Aug 20) and DXY is sliding (100.75 → 98.84 over 30 days); a hawkish tone signaling September hike despite soft growth would sharply pressure risk assets; a neutral or dovish tone alongside soft PCE would be the macro green light to extend BTC's rally (currently $77,416) toward new all-time highs; September 15–16 FOMC is the next binding commitment.
